chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Hassan! When a calamity befalls you, do not complain about it to anyone from the people of opposition (Ahl al-Khilaf), but mention it to one of your brothers, for you will not lack one of four qualities: either sufficiency by wealth, or assistance by prestige, or a supplication that is answered, or consultation by opinion.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْخِلَافِ: People of opposition (historically referring to the Umayyad caliphs or their loyalists)

ai.seo_question: What are the four ways a brother can help when you share your calamity with him according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs Hassan ibn Rashid to avoid venting to the 'people of opposition' (Ahl al-Khilaf), a term often referring to the Umayyad authorities or their political rivals, to prevent potential betrayal or superficial sympathy. Instead, he advises sharing troubles with a trusted brother, who will provide one of four forms of support: financial aid, social prestige, an answered prayer, or wise counsel. This guidance highlights the Shia emphasis on selective disclosure and the communal support system within the faithful during times of hardship.
